## What is an EOR Service?


An Employer of Record (EOR) is a third-party company that becomes the legal employer of your workers on paper, while you retain day-to-day control. The EOR handles payroll, taxes, benefits, and local compliance. Hiring someone in Brazil or India normally means setting up a local legal entity: months of work and tens of thousands of dollars. An EOR already has that entity, so your new hire is working in days.


What the EOR takes off your plate (including[local tax withholding and statutory benefits](https://nativeteams.com/blog/employer-of-record-benefits) ):


- Employment contracts drafted to meet local legal requirements
- Tax withholding and remittance to the appropriate authorities
- Statutory benefits mandated by the country of employment
- Termination procedures, which vary widely and carry real financial penalties if mishandled


This is general information, not legal advice. Rules vary by situation and change over time, so consult a qualified employment lawyer for your specific circumstances.


## How We Ranked EOR Services for Speed


We analyzed each provider using publicly available documentation, verified user reviews, industry benchmarks, and case studies. The core metrics we weighted:


- Time from offer acceptance to signed employment contract
- Contract generation and compliance processing speed
- Payroll setup timeline before first pay cycle
- Total days from offer to employee start date


We factored in how each provider performs across both straightforward and high-complexity markets. According to[global onboarding trends for 2026](https://www.ews-limited.com/global-onboarding-trends-2026-eor-onboarding-compliance/) , top performers complete the full process in under five business days, a sharp differentiator for startups where every week of delay has a direct cost.

## Remote


Remote covers EOR services, global payroll, and contractor management across 100+ countries through wholly-owned legal entities. That structure helps with compliance consistency but slows expansion into newer markets.


### What They Offer


- EOR hiring in 100+ countries through owned entities
- Global payroll for employees and contractors with local tax calculations
- Contractor management with built-in misclassification protection
- Compliance management aligned to local labor laws
- Benefits administration for international teams
- Self-serve onboarding via their dashboard with locally compliant employment contracts


Remote suits teams that want a well-documented, self-serve experience. The tradeoff: you still need to source candidates separately and manage interviews elsewhere.


Good for: Compliance-focused teams in markets with strict labor laws where misclassification risk is a concern.


Limitation: Onboarding runs 5 to 10 business days, stretching to 12 in markets like Brazil.


## Papaya Global


Papaya Global positions itself as a workforce payments and compliance solution, covering payroll management and HR across 160+ countries.


### What They Offer


- Global payroll processing with local tax calculations spanning 160 countries
- EOR services covering employment contracts, payroll, and benefits for international hires
- Contractor and workforce classification tools
- Compliance monitoring across multiple jurisdictions
- HR analytics across jurisdictions
- Fintech-style payments layer that consolidates global payroll into a single funding flow


Papaya is built around payroll accuracy and compliance reporting for finance-driven teams managing large distributed workforces. The interface leans toward audit trails over speed. When adding a new country, the typical process involves a configuration and compliance review period before payroll goes live, which can take several weeks depending on the market. Pricing starts at $650 or more per employee per month based on published rates. One concrete differentiator is their automated payroll funding workflow, which consolidates multi-currency payroll disbursements into a single funding instruction, reducing the back-and-forth that finance teams normally manage manually. Smaller teams often find setup involves more configuration than expected, and there is no recruiting layer.


Good for: Enterprises with 500+ employees across 10+ countries needing consolidated payroll reporting.


Limitation: Enterprise deployments run 2 to 4 months, a long runway compared to providers who get global payroll running in days.


## Multiplier


Multiplier is a Singapore-based EOR provider built for mid-size companies expanding into Asia-Pacific and other markets. It covers[EOR hiring and contractor management](https://www.bolto.com/blog/best-eor-companies-global-hiring-guide) across 150+ countries, with strong pricing for teams watching cost per hire. The product focuses on compliance and payroll execution once you have a candidate ready, but does not include any recruiting capability.


### What They Offer


- EOR services across 150+ countries with local currency payroll support
- Contractor management and compliance tools for international hires
- Benefits administration built into the hiring flow
- Onboarding employees in most countries within three to five business days, with 48 to 72 hours in owned-entity markets where Multiplier holds direct legal infrastructure
- EOR pricing at $400/month per employee, the most affordable published rate among providers with 150+ country coverage
- Statutory benefits administration covering health insurance, pension contributions, social security, and paid leave
- ESOP management support for companies offering equity compensation to international hires


Multiplier fits mid-size teams looking for straightforward international hiring without heavy enterprise configuration. Like most standalone EOR providers, it picks up after you've found your candidate. Sourcing and interviews stay on your plate.


Good for: Cost-conscious startups hiring in major markets.


Limitation: Three core integrations (BambooHR, Greenhouse, Workday) handle basics. Teams running Lever, NetSuite, or Slack will hit gaps.


## Oyster


Oyster HR covers[EOR hiring and payroll across 180+ countries](https://www.bolto.com/blog/global-employer-of-record-provider-guide) with compliance tools for local laws, benefits, and contractor management.


### What They Offer


- EOR services in 180+ countries with locally compliant contracts
- Global payroll with local currency support and taxes, deductions, and payments in local currencies
- Benefits packages aligned to statutory requirements by country, with localized benefits packages tailored to each country's requirements
- Contractor management with misclassification guidance
- Employment contracts with digital signing built into the onboarding flow
- Select markets support onboarding in as little as 48 hours


Oyster is designed for remote-first teams with a clean interface. Country-specific compliance guidance surfaces during onboarding. The ceiling shows up fast for startups moving quickly. Recruiting sits outside the product, and support quality has been inconsistent in complex markets.


Good for: Companies with defined hiring plans wanting high-touch support during first international hires.


Limitation: Detailed compliance checks slow contractor onboarding in restricted markets like the UK, France, and Germany.


## G-P (Globalization Partners)


G-P (Globalization Partners) is one of the longest-running names in[global employment](https://www.bolto.com/blog/eor-international-global-hiring-expansion-guide) , operating across 180 countries with owned entities in all major markets.


### What They Offer


- EOR coverage in 180 countries with 100% owned-entity infrastructure across all markets, removing partner coordination delays that slow competitors down
- Global compliance management covering local labor laws, statutory benefits, and tax obligations
- Payroll processing for international employees without requiring local entities
- Locally compliant contracts, payroll, and statutory benefits
- Dedicated compliance and legal support teams


G-P fits large enterprises with complex multi-country hiring needs. The compliance depth is real. The tradeoff is pace: onboarding runs longer than newer providers, and pricing is enterprise-level. No recruiting layer means sourcing happens before G-P enters the picture.


Good for: Enterprises where compliance failure carries real consequences like labor audits, wrongful termination claims, and works council disputes.


Limitation: Onboarding runs 5 to 15 business days where competitors finish in 2 to 3. No self-serve contract flow means every engagement starts with a sales conversation.

## FAQ


### How do I choose the right EOR service for my startup?


Start by identifying your biggest hiring bottleneck: if it's finding qualified candidates quickly, you need an EOR with built-in recruiting like Bolto. If you already have sourcing handled and just need compliant contracts, a standalone EOR provider like Remote works fine. Then match your budget to country coverage. Cheaper options often use partner entities in some markets, which can slow things down.


### Which EOR provider works best for companies hiring their first international employee?


Providers with owned entities and fast onboarding timelines make the first hire less risky. Bolto and G-P both operate through owned infrastructure, though G-P's enterprise pricing and longer setup might not fit early-stage budgets. Oyster and Multiplier offer cleaner interfaces for first-time users, but you'll still need to source candidates separately before their compliance work begins.


### Can an EOR service help me hire someone in less than one week?


Yes, but only if the provider handles both recruiting and compliance. Bolto delivers candidate shortlists in 72 hours and completes onboarding in 48 hours, putting someone to work in under five days total. Standalone EOR providers like Multiplier can onboard in two to five days, but that clock only starts after you have already found and vetted your candidate.


### What happens if I need to fire an international employee hired through an EOR?


The EOR generally handles termination procedures according to local labor law, including notice periods, severance calculations, and final pay timing that vary by country. In many jurisdictions, such as Brazil, local law generally requires around 30 days notice plus FGTS-related severance obligations, while at-will markets tend to move faster. In most arrangements, the EOR manages the legal process, while you retain the decision and communicate performance issues directly to the employee.


### Why do some EOR services cost $400 per month while others charge $800?


Pricing reflects infrastructure ownership, country coverage depth, and included services. Multiplier's $400 rate uses partner entities in many markets and offers minimal integrations. G-P's $800 rate buys owned entities in all 180+ countries and dedicated compliance teams. If recruiting, payroll, and compliance are bundled under one roof, expect pricing somewhere in between with faster end-to-end timelines.
